review.verdict:
LENS P (scope-materialisation): CORRECTIONS REQUIRED BEFORE SOURCE ACCEPTANCE. No P0 or P1 found in this lens. I found three P2 source corrections inside the lens (P-1, P-2, P-3), one cross-lens P2 reported so it is not lost (P-11), and seven P3 precision items.

What is sound (source behaviour reasoned from the bytes and the PostgreSQL 17 docs; NOT RUN):
- The narrow carrier stores raw bytes only for bindings and configuration, with size bounds.
- Each payload's full-raw SHA-256 must match both the publication entry and the decision entry before decoding.
- The closed read sets, recursive duplicate-key refusal and the depth, count and string bounds are present.
- No catalog, reconciliation or Health legal contents enter SQL.
- scope_members has the required row kinds, primary key, both partial uniques and all seven indexes, and no foreign keys to mutable parents.
- The header is inserted last with row counts and the rows digest. ALWAYS immutability triggers are in place, plus the named BEFORE INSERT seal once a header exists.
- One static resolver (derive/verify/offer/membership) is used by publish, activation, the strict reader, the commit's offer/witness resolution and the guard's OLD/NEW membership.
- Unresolved bindings refuse publication before any revision or head effect.
- Sealed OLD provenance is consulted first; a missing parent refuses (the registered cascade policy); new descendants are detected through sealed P/V/L/D or a visible chain; a visible parent with NULL or out-of-scope identity resolves OUT.
- Stock is request-only: one allocatable witness per variant, existence check only, no quantity aggregation, no inventory write.
- No regression against 25858ad: the publication and decision validators are byte-unchanged, read_current_authority is unchanged, and head/revision history refusal is preserved.

Blocking corrections:
- P-1: the required-input record_id refusal turns platform writes into permanent, unregistered 55000 refusals, including for out-of-scope domains.
- P-2: the carried CC-15-TYPES condition is unmet. Types are unqualified in the scope DDL, the resolver and the SECURITY DEFINER guard path, and that path is exposed to pg_temp type shadowing.
- P-3: the verifier has no negative controls for the carrier, the post-header INSERT seal or scope-table immutability, and this gap is not disclosed.

Everything else is precision that travels. Authored controls are not pass counts. Status remains LOCAL ONLY / NOT RUN / SOURCE ACCEPTANCE PENDING.

findings.title: Required-input record_id refusal makes platform writers fail permanently after first publication, including OUT domains
findings.claim: Membership raises 55000 for any changed research_required_inputs row whose record_id is non-null. The raise happens before the domain check, so it also fires for rows in unselected domains. Because revoke never clears last_published_revision_id, the refusal persists for the life of the installation. Under R3 (MD:727-729), resolution errors should fail publication, not platform writers. The event matrix says OUT rows bypass, and R2-16 only required stating that the selector is outside this profile. The source's own comment says domain membership is complete for this profile. The refusal is not registered under decision 3 and has no control.
findings.evidence: src SQL:916-921 (raise at :919-920 precedes the domain check at :921). The guard passes record_id at :1109 and uses last_published_revision_id at :1024 and :1113. Revoke keeps last_published (:1760-1761). record_id is a base column (supabase/research-required-input-readiness.sql:19@9c1c92b), set by the canonical define writer from recordId (:273-307@9c1c92b). The commit reads required inputs by domain only (intake.sql:678-687@9c1c92b). The verifier has no record_id control (grep).
findings.failureScenario: After the first synthetic or real publication, an operator defines or verifies a required input with recordId set in any domain, for example a product-record requirement used by the persistent-cart readiness path. The AFTER statement guard raises 55000 and the canonical command rolls back. There is no way to restore writability short of changing the installed source.
findings.fix: Classify research_required_inputs by sealed domain only, as the comment at :917-918 already states, and remove the record_id raise. If desired, also treat a record_id equal to a sealed product id as IN, conservatively. Add IN and OUT controls with non-null record_id. Alternatively, keep the refusal but register it as a decision-3 consequence and add explicit controls.

findings.title: Carried CC-15-TYPES unmet: unqualified types and casts in the scope DDL, resolver and SECURITY DEFINER guard path
findings.claim: R3 MD:762 and section 13 carry the requirement to schema-qualify all types, casts and row types under an empty search_path, with pg_temp shadowing negatives. The currentness scope objects use bare uuid, text, jsonb, bigint, bytea and numeric, and bare ::uuid casts. The intake family qualifies them (pg_catalog.uuid). The PG17 docs say that with an empty search_path the temporary schema is still searched first for data type names. Doc78 C-1 requires proconfig to be exactly search_path="", so qualification is the only remedy.
findings.evidence: Carrier and members DDL at src SQL:389-401 and :423-436. Resolver declarations (uuid[], text[], uuid) at :729-737. Casts (item->>'id')::uuid at :908-941. Guard declarations at :983-990; guard is SECURITY DEFINER (:982) and calls the resolver as owner (:1113). Intake contrast: pg_catalog.uuid[] at intake.sql:331 and ::pg_catalog.uuid at :589-590. Docs: runtime-config-client 'search_path' says the temp schema is searched first if not listed, for relation and data type names (NOT RUN). sql-createfunction 'Writing SECURITY DEFINER Functions Safely'.
findings.failureScenario: Reasoned, NOT RUN. A session with TEMPORARY privilege creates a pg_temp domain named uuid or jsonb whose CHECK calls a pg_temp function, then performs a guarded write. The definer guard and resolver resolve the shadowed type, and the CHECK function runs with the owner's privileges, or the guard errors. Exploitation needs a principal with direct SQL access and a write path to a guarded relation. That is outside the disclosed trust model, so this is rated P2, not P0.
findings.fix: Qualify every type, cast and row type as pg_catalog.* in the scope tables, resolve_scope, the guard, publish, activation and the strict reader, matching the intake family's convention. Add the pg_temp shadowing negative controls named in R3 MD:762.

findings.fix: Author the listed refusal controls (NOT RUN), each asserting no head, revision or member change. At minimum, add the seal trigger and U/D/T controls, and record any intentionally deferred ones in the receipt's remaining list.

findings.title: Tests child rule omits the sealed-L step used by the documents rule (R2-15 'one rule per child relation, identical')
findings.claim: Documents resolve IN through sealed D or sealed L before the live chain. Tests use sealed D and then the live document-to-lot P/V chain, without checking whether the document's lot is in sealed L. A test under an unsealed document on a sealed lot whose live P/V left the selection would resolve OUT while its document resolves IN. This is unreachable while the head is active: lot identity changes in L are material and closure changes refuse re-activation. So this is precision, not fail-open.

findings.claim: resolve_scope 'offer' returns lotIds and documentIds whose sealed product OR variant matches. The commit then applies a separate live product AND variant equality to pick the witness. The result is conservative, but the admissible-witness mapping is split across two implementations instead of the single shared mapping R3 MD:713-715 describes.
findings.evidence: src SQL:892-893; intake.sql:588-591 and :719@9c1c92b.
findings.fix: Have 'offer' return the exact-variant admissible witness candidate set, sealed lot rows with product_id=P and variant_id=V and their documents, or state in both bodies that the exact-variant narrowing is the Decision-2 stock rule applied on top of the shared mapping.

verdicts.note: Confirmed from the bytes. At src SQL:919-920 any changed research_required_inputs identity with a non-null record_id raises 55000 before the domain test at :921, whatever the domain. The guard reaches membership whenever last_published_revision_id is set (:1024, :1113), and revoke never clears that column (:1760-1761). Doc73 CC-4 (73:113-118) names exactly this as the defect its fix was meant to remove: an unresolved selector 'refuses every material platform write once any revision is published', and the fix is that 'an unresolvable identifier then fails publication, not platform writers'. The commit reads required inputs only by domain: intake.sql:680 and :685@9c1c92b, plus research_domain_readiness and the manifest hash in research-required-input-readiness.sql:208-250 and :474-531@9c1c92b, all filtered by domain. So an OUT-domain row with a record_id is never read, and refusing it buys no protection. The matrix's 'uncertain scope refuse' column does not cover this case, because R2-16 puts the selector outside this profile. The failure is closed (availability), not open. The verifier has no record_id case (grep).

Confirmed. Neither base/ nor src/ uses pg_catalog-qualified types anywhere (grep returns 0). The SECURITY DEFINER guard declares bare text/uuid/jsonb/bigint/numeric/oid (src SQL:983-990) and assigns marker (:1016) and revision (:1024) before any integrity call. resolve_scope uses bare uuid[]/text[] and ::uuid casts (:729-737, :908-941). R3 MD:762 and section 13 CC-15-TYPES (MD:1084) carry the qualification requirement to this source, and R3 MD:707 specifies pg_catalog.* types. By the PG docs, with search_path='' the temp schema is searched first for type names (reasoned, NOT RUN). If a non-owner principal with TEMP privilege and direct SQL DML on any guarded table exists, a pg_temp domain CHECK would run with the owner's rights, which must be rolsuper or rolbypassrls (:564). R3 MD:634-636 expressly anticipates low-privilege writers firing the definer guard. Installation is impossible in this source (expected_columns:=null at :1985-1998; the seal constant is null at :555-558), so nothing is enabled today. P2 stands; the reviewer should treat it as escalation-class before any installable successor.

Confirmed. src SQL:4 and :129-131 still state the S0 'metadata only' and 'SQL does not read artifacts' readings beside the derive parser at :784-803. Doc76:49 cites exactly these lines as the disclosed departure. R3 MD:692 ties their update to the authorised successor, and Decision 5 (bfe7f27 DIRECT_AUTHORITY:62) grants Part 2. No comment names the intake header-verifying call. intake.sql@9c1c92b mentions resolve_scope only at :580 and :870, and verification actually happens through the strict reader's verify at src SQL:970. This is comment-only.

Refuted on the requirement. R3 MD:717 defines the rules separately: 'new documents via sealedL or a proven live lot->P/V chain, new tests via sealedD or proven document->lot->P/V chain'. Matrix row MD:842 defines tests as 'quality_document_id in D', then the shared resolver. The source implements exactly that (src SQL:935-942). In R2-15 (R3 MD:1136) 'identical' means the same rule stated identically in the MD matrix, MD:696 and the JSON rows. It does not require the documents and tests rules to be identical to each other. The lens itself concedes the scenario cannot occur while the head is active (closure equality at :1943-1947). Not a defect.

Refuted on the requirement. R3 MD:715 says the save must 'Compare live typed projections and locked witnesses against this same mapping and actual approved stock rule'. So the design itself places the stock-rule comparison in the commit, applied to the resolver's sealed mapping. intake.sql:587-591@9c1c92b filters sealed lotIds by exact live P/V and allocatability, which is that comparison, and the result is never broader than the sealed set. Any lot identity change in L is material and holds the head, so live and sealed P/V agree under an active head. An explanatory comment would be harmless but is not a correction.

What conforms, checked against the bytes at 9c1c92b:
- The guard is VOLATILE SECURITY DEFINER with proconfig exactly search_path="". It has no EXECUTE grants, uses no dynamic SQL, and its relations and functions are schema-qualified.

- The candidate and rollback inventories agree: 47 triggers, 13 functions and 6 tables. The rollback refuses while the intake family is present or while used evidence exists.

- integrity() can never pass after install, because its owned-relation predicate also matches the family's own indexes.
- The required structural checks on the 12 IN relations are missing in every phase: relkind, inheritance or partition, rules, and subscription target.
- CC-15-TYPES is unmet: types, casts and catalog relations are unqualified under an empty search_path.

- CC-17 (the alias-free cross-alias legal-binding INSERT case) is not implemented.
- The verifier asserts the old head-trigger behaviour and lacks several required controls.

findings.failureScenario: Once a successor binds the descriptor (sql:555, 1985), every integrity() caller raises 55000. Effects: no material write can complete, no authority can be published or activated, and an installed family cannot be rolled back with the reviewed block. It fails closed, but no positive control can ever pass.

Keep indexes under the fingerprint only. Add a reapply/postcheck positive control and an RLS-disabled negative control on a new table.

findings.title: Structural predicates for the 12 IN relations are missing in all four phases
findings.claim: R3 requires that precheck, reapply, postcheck and runtime integrity all verify each of the 12 source relations has relkind 'r', no pg_inherits parent or child (which also covers partitions), no rewrite rules, and no pg_subscription_rel entry. None of these predicates exists, apart from relkind at install and inside the guard. The precheck's absent branch checks nothing about the source relations.
findings.evidence: There are no pg_inherits or pg_subscription_rel references in src. pg_rewrite is read only for owned_relations (sql:82-83). relkind appears only at sql:1997 (install count, NULL-gated) and sql:1012 (per-trigger, when the guard fires). integrity() (sql:553-720) and precheck/postcheck (101-148) omit them. R3 MD:753-761. PG17 CREATE TRIGGER notes say statement-level triggers fire only on the explicitly named table, not on its partitions or child tables.
findings.failureScenario: Suppose a source relation becomes a partition or inheritance child (its relkind stays 'r') or gains a DO INSTEAD rule, through owner DDL or a prior migration. Writes routed through the parent or the rule then never fire that relation's statement guard. Canonical readers that select from the parent see the changed rows, yet the epoch never advances and integrity() and the strict reader still pass. A save could then rely on stale authority. This is not P0 only because it needs owner-level DDL (the CC-16 trust boundary); these checks are the required detection.
findings.fix: Add one identical predicate block for exactly the 12 relations to integrity(), both install-block branches, precheck (including its absent branch) and postcheck. The block should require: relkind='r'; not relispartition; no pg_inherits row with inhrelid or inhparent in the set; no pg_rewrite row; no pg_subscription_rel row. Author a negative control for each.

With search_path='' and pg_temp unlisted, the session's temp schema is searched first for relation and type names, including inside SECURITY DEFINER code. findings.evidence: Guard: sql:983, 1007, 1010-1011, 1020, 1027, 1112. Strict reader: 974-975. Resolver: 808-819, 908-941. integrity(): 639-640, 649, 655-659, 667, 677-678, 690, 706, 710. fingerprint_sql: 61-84, repeated in precheck and postcheck. findings.failureScenario: A writer or intake session creates temp tables named pg_trigger, pg_class or pg_attribute, or temp types named jsonb, uuid or regclass, before its statement. In guard paths this yields cast or parse errors, which are refusals and fail closed. In the strict reader, called by the definer commit, forged catalog rows can make integrity() and schema_fingerprint() pass despite real drift, for example a disabled guard trigger. That masking requires owner-level drift as well.
findings.fix: Qualify every type and cast in all currentness bodies, DO blocks and rollback as pg_catalog.jsonb, uuid, text, name, oid, regclass, regprocedure, regnamespace, regrole, regcollation, timestamptz and bytea. verdicts.note: Confirmed at src sql:702-705, where there is no relkind filter and relkind<>'r' and missing RLS sit inside the failure disjunction. PostgreSQL auto-names these indexes with the 38-character prefix research_health_quick_order_authority_: revisions_pkey (sql:347), head_pkey (sql:359), activations_pkey and the writer_epoch unique key (sql:408, 413), revocations_pkey and its unique key (sql:417-418), and scope_members_pkey (sql:437). The two writer_epoch key names exceed 63 characters, and the NAMEDATALEN truncation shortens the table-name portion while keeping the prefix. All are relkind 'i' with relrowsecurity false, so once sql:557 stops raising, integrity() always raises 55000. The predicate is new since 25858ad; the base has only the relkind-filtered ACL loop at base sql:482. Every caller is affected: install sql:2046, the precheck and postcheck present branch :120, the strict reader sql:956, the guard sql:1116, publish, revoke and activate, and rollback.md:222. It fails closed, but no positive path can ever pass.

Confirmed. src has no pg_inherits, pg_subscription_rel or relispartition reference. pg_rewrite is read only for owned_relations (sql:83). relkind appears only at sql:1997 and in the per-fire guard check at sql:1012. The precheck absent branch (precheck:101-148) checks nothing. R3 MD:753-761 requires all four predicates in every phase. Docs 17 confirm the mechanism. CREATE TRIGGER notes: statement-level triggers fire only on the explicitly named table, not on its partitions or children. logical-replication-architecture: 'The logical replication apply process currently only fires row triggers, not statement triggers.' So a subscription target bypasses all 47 statement guards, even though they are ENABLE ALWAYS. Each path needs owner-equivalent power: table ownership for INHERIT, ATTACH or RULE; for a subscription, superuser or pg_create_subscription plus SET ROLE to the table owner. That keeps it at P2 under CC-16. Also, the correction map has no row tracking these R3 structural predicates.

Confirmed against R3 MD:762. That text also requires builtins to be qualified, which the lens fix omits. Unqualified builtins include count(*) (sql:772, 810, 831, 876, 887, 1593), pg_get_userbyid, obj_description, to_regprocedure, aclexplode, acldefault and has_*_privilege in integrity() (sql:639-715), jsonb_build_object (sql:1962), and encode, convert_to, format_type and pg_get_* in fingerprint_sql. PG17 runtime-config-client confirms that an unlisted pg_temp is searched first for relation and type names, never for functions or operators. I tried to build a fail-open from type shadowing. In the guard and resolver paths, a temp domain, enum or composite named jsonb, uuid or regclass gives a cast or operator error, which fails closed. In the strict reader, a temp domain over pg_catalog.timestamp named timestamptz under a non-UTC approved TimeZone would shift the effectiveUntil comparison (sql:974-975). However, valid_publication (sql:107-112), called first at sql:964, round-trips the same casts through to_char in the session TimeZone and returns false for any non-zero offset. I could not construct a working bypass. Masking integrity() or the fingerprint still needs owner-level drift, so the severity is unchanged.

Confirmed. sql:1035 removes every alias-free INSERT row, and membership treats every legal row as scoped (sql:924-925). intake.sql:566 at 9c1c92b takes FOR SHARE only on the row it resolved, so a concurrently committed alias-free row B with customer_ref Y neither conflicts nor advances the epoch, and the post-gate checks do not re-resolve the legal mapping. R3 rated CC-17 P3 only as a carried source-acceptance criterion (MD:876, 1082). The source successor does not implement it, so it is a required source correction (P2). The verifier (mjs:779-786) and the correction map (ev:2939-2942) record the bypass as an expected positive control, contrary to R3's 'source gap not accepted'.

Confirmed. Under src sql:499-503, a gateless head UPDATE raises 'exclusive authority gate required' before any FK check, because FK checks are AFTER triggers. mjs:2051-2063 therefore expects the wrong message and wrong successes. mjs:2069-2071 and 2076-2078 can never see 23503. mjs:2084-2085 throws. mjs:1546-1549 gets the same SQLSTATE with a different message, so refused() fails at mjs:278. Only one function's proconfig is inventoried (mjs:330, against C-1's matching verifier inventory). There are no guard-drift, MERGE, writable-CTE, COPY, pg_temp or structural controls (grep finds none), and the drift list (mjs:2107-2119) and role loop (2093-2105) cover only the old objects. Additional precision: doc71GuardInventory (mjs:637) uses an unescaped LIKE 'research_health_quick_order_guard_%'. That is broader than integrity's escaped predicate. All of this sits behind mjs:496/1485 and is NOT RUN.

Confirmed. sql:631-636 has no tgattr or tgqual predicate. The five new history and seal triggers and the three new FKs are bound only through the install-time fingerprint snapshot (sql:66-73, 2042-2044). The fingerprint reads unqualified pg_trigger, so an explicit predicate against pg_catalog.pg_trigger would also be independent of R-3. There is no bypass without owner drift.

Confirmed. The loop at sql:2033-2039 has no namespace filter and formats public.%I. A foreign prefixed trigger causes a 42P01 or 42704 error, or a stray comment, followed by the integrity raise at sql:2046 and a full rollback, so it fails closed. The precheck absent branch also misses a foreign prefixed trigger whose function is not in the family, because `present` is false. That breaks R3 MD:646 'refuse precheck'.

Upheld; stage adjusted from S3. The rollback half (rollback.md:223-225 detects only commit(jsonb) and the intakes table) is in the reviewed currentness family and is a precision fix to make now. The intake-gate half (intake.sql:860-871 compares only seal part 2 and two signatures) travels to the dependent intake reseal. Note the rollback also calls integrity() first (rollback.md:222), so R-1 blocks it entirely.

Confirmed at sql:1217/1227 and the copies in publish, revoke and activate (1515/1525, 1879/1889). PostgreSQL displays a time GUC in the largest unit that divides it exactly, so 60000ms reads back as 1min and refuses. Doc78 C-2 allows refusing 'an unsupported unit' if the profile contract records the restriction. The fixture values (mjs:542-546) happen to be whole seconds. The dead 'writer'='intake' branch (sql:1237) is harmless, because Doc78 section 3 applies lock < deadlock to intake only. Guard seal identity is checked by format only (sql:1016-1018).

Valid carried condition. The full-row to_jsonb paths (sql:1084-1108) render float through float8out, which follows extra_float_digits. OLD and NEW are rendered under the same setting within one statement, but a lossy rendering can collapse distinct values. There is no present float column. Not refuted.

review.verdict:
Lens S (settings, admission and trust), read-only, NOTHING RUN. I found no P0 or P1 in the currentness family at source 9c1c92bcb7a514da9b575a291d0abac67c8ba366, judged against the Doc78 conditions in my scope (C-1 to C-5, C-7, C-9, C-11, C-12).

**What holds.** The guard, publish, revoke and activate functions each carry the same admission block (src:1119-1249, 1417-1560, 1618-1752, 1781-1926). Each block, before the gate or head:
- reads the effective lock, statement, transaction, idle and deadlock timers with their units;
- refuses values that are absent or zero, in an unsupported unit, overflowing or above their field;
- enforces idle < statement < transaction, intake lock < deadlock, writer gate >= intake transaction + cleanup, and remaining budget at the gate >= gate + reserve;
- requires catalog equality for the exact login role and database;
- reads back the login and request roles and checks owner OID equality;
- computes budgets from transaction_timestamp().

The guard runs this block even before publication. The anchor is a comment on the scope-inputs relation: owner-supplied, never set by this source, excluded from the fingerprint, and refusing when absent. It is not a settings table, a caller setting, a writer edit or a compiled digest. The digest contract in the shared bindings record has no cycle, and that record holds no successor or receipt digest. Both receipts are PENDING, and their 87-file inventories are byte-identical.

The base installer timer settings (`SET LOCAL lock_timeout '5s'` and `statement_timeout '60s'`) are removed. There is no plain SET, no fake receipt and no claim of pre-BEGIN arming. Since the lease was recorded (3f7601d), the only edits are the 17 source paths, the 4 evidence paths and .xenios coordination records; no excluded path was edited.

**Corrections before acceptance.**
- **S-1 (P2, S2):** the verifier has no function-settings inventory that matches the integrity function, which C-1 requires.
- **S-2 (P2, S2):** a new compiled maximum, `quantity not between 1 and 100`, appears in the intake commit. It belongs to the intake reseal and does not block currentness acceptance.

**Limits that travel (P3).**
- One anchor admits only one route identity.
- The anchor cannot be supplied inside the installation transaction.
- Only ms and s units are accepted.
- The writer and admin SQL paths do not enforce the canonical byte form.
- A LIKE wildcard is used where an exact prefix match is meant.
- Several refusal classes have no control.
- Some receipt and comment wording is imprecise.

**Recommendation:** source acceptance with limits for the currentness family, once S-1 is corrected or explicitly waived. The definition digest 6c6b27b4… is consistent across records, but I did not recompute it, so it is NOT PROVEN. Execution and operation are not established.

findings.title: CC-17 alias-free cross-alias insert has no positive/negative controls and no stage in the map

findings.title: QC02 'before-mutation' and QC03 'nine increments roll back' are not discriminated by their assertions
findings.claim: Head and snapshot equality after a refused statement is guaranteed by PostgreSQL statement atomicity whether the canonical check runs before or after the upserts. QC02 cannot show 'before mutation', and QC03's rollback assertion cannot fail on any QO source change.

findings.title: Future-binding gate misses integrity()'s NULL seal; message-less historical refusals accept any 55000

findings.title: Effective timer parser accepts only ms/s, and fixtures avoid minute multiples (reasoned, NOT RUN)

Synthetic values 1s, 7s, 15s and 20s never exercise this, so an approved minute-multiple profile would fail closed with no control showing it.

findings.title: Fixture idle-in-transaction timeout of 1s applies to holder/observer sessions; gate and revoke controls depend on sub-second scheduling

verdicts.note: Confirmed in the bytes. src mjs:951 revokes with 'synthetic revocation' (contains a space). revoke_revision refuses at SQL:1745-1746: the reason must match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$, else 22023. R2-4 (r3 MD:1104) and r3 MD:653-655 add the concurrent publish/activation RR/SER writers. READ UNCOMMITTED is discriminable: current_setting returns 'read uncommitted', which SQL:995 refuses. No profile mutation is ever combined with 'active-synthetic', publish, activation or revoke (grep: the only active-synthetic contexts are mjs:931 and mjs:946, both with a valid profile). r3 MD:659/661 and MD:1106-1112, plus Doc78 C-8 (78:194-198), require these controls. The source predicates exist (SQL:1197-1200), but no approved-field negative other than null/0 is authored. See TV-3 for the uncontrolled relation predicates.

Confirmed. The remaining lists (ev map:753-806, 4274-4287) carry no stage. grep finds no MERGE, writable-CTE, COPY or foreign/disabled prefix-trigger entry in the map or the verifier, although r3 MD:763-768 lists them. revoke-with-source-lock, immutable-revocation-evidence and revoked-reactivation-refusal are listed without caveat (ev map:3147-3183), and the receipt lists them as acceptance evidence. The source regex accepts only ms|s (SQL:1217, 1227), and the fixture values (7s/15s/20s/1s) avoid minute multiples. That PostgreSQL shows 60000ms as '1min' is NOT PROVEN from documentation. The config-setting page (www.postgresql.org/docs/17/config-setting.html) describes input-unit conversion only, so this display behaviour is reasoned, not documented. Fail-closed. upheld.claim:

- In the definer guard, a session-created temp domain named jsonb, text or uuid whose CHECK calls an explicitly qualified pg_temp function would run that function as the owner, which :564 requires to be rolsuper or rolbypassrls. The CHECK fires on the first assignment, before any bypass.

Exploitation needs a principal with TEMP privilege and direct SQL DML on a guarded relation; the census marks such routes UNPROVEN, and nothing is installable now. So this stays P2, but it is a hard blocker before any installable successor.

Qualify every non-keyword type and cast as pg_catalog.* (jsonb, uuid, text, name, oid, bytea, regclass, regprocedure, regnamespace, regrole, regcollation, timestamptz), and every catalog relation and builtin as pg_catalog.*. (a) A temp domain with a CHECK that calls a pg_temp marker function, followed by a guarded zero-row UPDATE and a material UPDATE. The marker must never execute as owner.
(b) Temp pg_class/pg_trigger tables created before integrity and the strict reader. The integrity outcome must be unchanged.
